What Payment Base provides
Four pillars · one PSP-agnostic core
The provider-agnostic core

Payment Base provides
four pillars.

Payment Base (oxid-esales/payment-base) is the layer below every PSP module (Stripe, PayPal, …), every returns flow (OpalReturns), and every shipping integration. PSPs and downstream modules never import each other — they share only Payment Base.

1

Admin “Payment” tab

One shared tab on the OXID admin Order Details page. PSPs contribute panels via a tagged service oe.payment.admin_panel — no per-PSP admin tabs.

2

Domain models

PaymentContract aggregate, BasketSnapshot value object, Transaction, ContractCondition, ContractState enum. Owns all 6 database tables.

3

Event system

PSR-14 EventDispatcher, request-scoped EventContext, HandlerInterface, 30+ events. Anyone can introduce a new event.

4

Smart-Contracts

State machine DRAFT → … → FULFILLED with extensible conditions (payment_authorized, fraud_check, …). Early-Order-Creation pattern out of the box.

Six abstract base classes. ContractCreationHandler, AbstractPaymentCaptureService, AbstractPaymentRefundService, AbstractWebhookProcessor, AbstractHandler, AbstractFileLoggerFactory — you extend, you don’t copy.
~25 interfaces. PaymentAdapterInterface, ShopAdapterInterface, SessionAdapterInterface, repository & service interfaces. The boundary rule — if it’s provider-agnostic, it lives here.
Architecture invariants. PSPs are peers. opalreturns is PSP-agnostic. No direct contract mutations in controllers. Grep guards in pre-commit enforce the lines.
